label: late original-phase input of v (and j/k/m after g/o earlier in the sequence)
explanation: Fires only during the original-input phase, never at t<2, on the delimiter, or during copy. Mostly a token detector: v carries 45% of activation mass (11x lift), then j, k, m (about 39% together), with weaker contributions from a, 1, b. Rate grows with position (orig_idx 8 is 8.5x lift, t=2 rare), and it fires mostly on the first occurrence of the token. Magnitude is higher when g or o appeared earlier, especially as the first token (first_tok g/o 4-5x lift); every top example is v late in a sequence that starts with g/o/r. Many v/j/k/m inputs late in a sequence still do not fire, so precision is low (about 0.34). Dev F1 0.42, mass recall 0.70. The dependence on context looks graded and hidden-state-like, not a clean rule.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: v, j, k, m, a, 1; least: 3, o, p, x) and the first original token (most: g, o, r, z, 3, x; least: j, k, m, v); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, t=5, t=4.
